technical_and_design_decisions: Target the historical Spring XD codebase and Spring Boot 1.1.x compatibility implied by the user stories, rather than Spring Framework 6, because the requirements explicitly reference Spring Boot 1.1.x and Java 7 Docker images.
Use the Spring Boot security starter and the property server.basic.enabled as the feature switch, with false as the application default.
Implement single-user credentials through servers.yml and adapt the XD server configuration to create the required Spring Security user configuration.
Extend the XD Shell admin config command with --username and --password options and use HTTP Basic authentication for requests to the secured admin server.
Treat the Spring Boot snapshot and release dependency requests as build and dependency-management changes, with compatibility validation against the existing project.

For the REST archive request, deliver only the specified spike outcome: customer assessment, option analysis, team-feedback material, phased proposal, and follow-up stories; do not implement the REST API.
Build the sandbox Docker image with Ubuntu, Java 7, the full XD distribution, Redis, and RabbitMQ, using a simple startup/configuration approach suitable for experimentation.
Build the production Docker image with Ubuntu, Java 7, and the full XD distribution, keeping Redis and RabbitMQ external to the image.
Use automated unit and integration tests where practical, supplemented by manual command-line and Docker smoke tests for container and authentication behavior.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD project builds successfully before the increment begins, and the developer has access to its source repository, build system, and test infrastructure.
No new authentication provider, database-backed user store, OAuth, TLS, or role-management model is required; authentication is limited to HTTP Basic and single-user credentials.
The servers.yml schema and configuration-loading mechanisms already exist and can be extended without a broad configuration migration.
The admin server and XD Shell communicate over HTTP using existing client abstractions that can be enhanced to add Basic Auth credentials.
The requested Spring Boot snapshot and release are compatible enough with the target branch to be evaluated through dependency updates; resolving unrelated upstream defects is out of scope.
Dockerfiles, startup scripts, and concise usage documentation are sufficient deliverables for both Docker images; publishing to a registry and production infrastructure deployment are out of scope.
The full XD JAR/distribution and required third-party artifacts are available to the Docker build, or can be referenced through the existing build output.
The REST API spike includes workshops or asynchronous team feedback but does not include implementation, deployment, or a production API contract.
Effort includes implementation, developer testing, documentation, and code review preparation, but excludes elapsed waiting time for external approvals or infrastructure provisioning.
All estimates are single most-likely work-hour estimates for one developer and are not calendar-duration estimates.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing Spring XD security, configuration, shell, build, distribution, and Docker-related structure; define the implementation approach and compatibility constraints for U1-U8.

activities.activity_name: Add optional Basic Auth dependency and property
activities.activity_description: Add the Spring Boot security starter, introduce server.basic.enabled, set its default to false in application.yml, and wire the conditional security behavior into the admin server.
Extend servers.yml parsing and server configuration so users can provide or override a single username and password, including validation, default handling, and integration with Spring Security.
Add --username and --password options to the admin config command, persist or pass the values to the admin client as appropriate, and configure HTTP Basic authentication on outgoing requests.

activities.activity_name: Update and validate Spring Boot snapshot dependency
activities.activity_description: Update build dependency management to consume the required latest Spring Boot snapshot, adjust repositories or build settings, resolve compatibility issues, and verify a clean build.

activities.activity_name: Update and validate Spring Boot release dependency
activities.activity_description: Update or provide the corresponding latest Spring Boot release dependency configuration, resolve version conflicts, and verify that the release-based build remains functional.
Add tests for disabled-by-default behavior, enabled Basic Auth challenges, valid and invalid credentials, servers.yml overrides, and XD Shell authenticated and unauthenticated admin requests.
Assess the customer need for uploading an archive containing custom module definitions and configurations; identify workflows, constraints, security concerns, and candidate technical options.

activities.activity_name: REST archive spike socialization and follow-up stories
activities.activity_description: Prepare and conduct team feedback activities, document decisions and trade-offs, identify implementation phases, and write the resulting follow-up stories and acceptance criteria.
Create the sandbox Dockerfile and startup/configuration scripts for Ubuntu, Java 7, the full XD JAR/distribution, Redis, and RabbitMQ; expose required ports and provide basic usage instructions.
Create a leaner production-oriented Dockerfile and startup configuration containing Ubuntu, Java 7, and the full XD JAR/distribution, with configuration hooks for externally managed services.

activities.activity_name: Docker smoke testing and image documentation
activities.activity_description: Build both images, verify startup and XD connectivity, test the sandbox service dependencies, check configuration and port behavior, and document build, run, and configuration procedures.

Run the complete build and test suite, perform cross-feature regression checks, update release notes or project documentation, address defects found during validation, and prepare the increment for review.
